## Distance effect vs region effect

The drop from the random split to blocks has two parts. The **distance** part is what thinning labels on a random split to the same median nearest-label distance costs (interpolated in log-distance from E1b). The **region** part is the remainder: what holding out whole regions costs beyond being that far from labels. Blocks of 500 and 1000 km (median distance ≈110 and ≈187 km) fall inside the E1b range (50–290 km).

## E3a/b/d: does the TTE lead survive a change of probe?

Same embeddings, same folds. TTE, SatCLIP L40 and gap (TTE minus SatCLIP L40) are means over all grid offsets (blocks) or seeds (random); 'ahead' counts the offsets or seeds where TTE scores higher. The CI is the 95% block bootstrap on offset 0 alone (seed 42 for random, by point), so it need not contain the mean gap. kNN on raw coordinates is the lookup baseline.

## E4 (added after E3, not pre-registered): where in TTE does linear readability appear?

Ridge probe (paper protocol) on each stage of the TTE location encoder, same folds. Stages: soft-Voronoi site embedding `w @ E` (384-d) → after semantic-register attention (512-d) → after the residual MLP, normalized (the released 512-d embedding). kNN on the released embedding is the readability ceiling.

Soft assignment: a location's effective number of sites (1/Σw²) has median 80 (10th–90th pct 30–152) and the largest single weight has median 0.050, on the global tasks. Recomputed final embeddings match the cached ones exactly (max |diff| 0).
